newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Tajik battle leaves 14 dead, siege said continuing.
newsitem.headline: Tajik battle leaves 14 dead, siege said continuing.

text.p: Fourteen people have been killed in a joint operation against a maverick Tajik guerrilla group mounted by government troops and their former foes in the Islamic opposition, a Tajik official said on Tuesday.

Gafur Mirzoyev, commander of the Tajik presidential guard, told Reuters by telephone from the capital, Dushanbe, that fighters led by Rizvon Sadirov were surrounded in the hills some 80 km (50 miles) east of Dushanbe. The battle was continuing.
Eight had been killed and five taken prisoner at a cost of three dead among the government troops and a further three among their allies in the official opposition forces, he said.

Mirzoyev estimated a further two days were needed to complete the operation, the first joint action between government and opposition since they agreed a ceasefire in December to settle a bitter four-year civil war.

The Tajik government, which is striving to control a country awash with arms and riven by factional interests, said on March 20 that it had launched an operation to destroy Sadirov's group, which it estimated to number about 40.

Sadirov once fought for the opposition. But his loyalties are now unclear. In December, he took a group of foreigners hostage. In February his brother held 14 foreign aid workers, military observers and journalists for two weeks.
